lessons.title: Equivalent fractions and simplest form

cards.title: What is a fraction?
cards.body: "The numbers of the form a/b, where a and b are natural numbers, are called fractions."
cards.reveal: In a/b, we call a the numerator and b the denominator.

cards.title: Numerator and denominator
cards.body: "In a/b, we call a the numerator and b the denominator."
cards.example: In 2/3, the numerator is 2 and the denominator is 3.

cards.title: Equivalent fractions
cards.body: "Two or more fractions representing the same part of a whole are called equivalent fractions."

cards.title: Making an equivalent fraction
cards.body: "To get a fraction equivalent to a given fraction, we multiply or divide the numerator and the denominator of the given fraction by the same nonzero number."
cards.reveal: Same number on top and bottom, and never zero.

cards.title: Simplest form
cards.body: Dividing the numerator and the denominator by the same number makes a fraction simpler. Your book says: "the simplest form of 21/35 is 3/5."

cards.title: Proper and improper fractions
cards.body: "A fraction whose numerator is less than its denominator is called a proper fraction; otherwise, it is called an improper fraction."

cards.title: Mixed fractions
cards.body: "A mixed fraction = A whole number + A fraction."
cards.example: Your book writes 9/8 = 1 1/8: one whole and 1/8 more.

cards.title: Mixed into improper
cards.body: Before adding, your book changes a mixed fraction into an improper fraction: 2 4/5 = 14/5.

keyRules: The numbers of the form a/b, where a and b are natural numbers, are called fractions. In a/b, we call a the numerator and b the denominator.
Two or more fractions representing the same part of a whole are called equivalent fractions.
To get a fraction equivalent to a given fraction, we multiply or divide the numerator and the denominator of the given fraction by the same nonzero number.
A fraction whose numerator is less than its denominator is called a proper fraction; otherwise, it is called an improper fraction.
A mixed fraction = A whole number + A fraction.

lessons.title: Comparing fractions: same denominator, same numerator, cross multiplication

videos.title: Comparing fractions by cross multiplication (parent to choose)

cards.title: Rule 1: same denominator
cards.body: "Among two fractions with the same denominator, the one with the greater numerator is the greater of the two."

cards.title: Why Rule 1 works
cards.body: 8/9 and 5/9 are both made of ninths. 8 ninths are more than 5 ninths, so 8/9 > 5/9.

cards.title: Rule 2: same numerator
cards.body: "Among two fractions with the same numerator, the one with the smaller denominator is the greater of the two."

cards.title: Why Rule 2 works
cards.body: Cut a cake into 6 parts and another into 8 parts. Each sixth is bigger than each eighth, so 5/6 > 5/8.

cards.title: Cross multiplication
cards.body: Let a/b and c/d be the two given fractions. Cross multiply, and find the cross products ad and bc.
cards.reveal: a × d on one side, b × c on the other

cards.title: Reading the cross products
cards.body: (i) If ad > bc then a/b > c/d. (ii) If ad < bc then a/b < c/d. (iii) If ad = bc then a/b = c/d.

cards.title: Example 2: 3/8 and 5/12
cards.body: By cross multiplying: 3 × 12 = 36 and 8 × 5 = 40. Clearly, 36 < 40.

cards.title: Example 3: 5/9 and 6/11
cards.body: By cross multiplying: 5 × 11 = 55 and 9 × 6 = 54. Clearly, 55 > 54.

cards.title: The short method
cards.body: Divide the LCM by each denominator, then multiply by the numerator: [36 ÷ 9 = 4, 4 × 8 = 32] and [36 ÷ 12 = 3, 3 × 5 = 15]. So 8/9 + 5/12 = (32 + 15)/36.
